newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses at close on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses at close on late buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks reined in earlier losses at the close of trade Monday on bargain buying after a session dominated by caution over the possible effect of U.S. elections on Mexican markets, traders said.
"Uncertainty persists regarding (Mexico's) budget proposals and the outcome of the U.S. elections," said Esteban Rojas, deputy research director at Arka brokerage firm in Mexico City.
The blue chip IPC index ended down 8.11 points, or 0.25 percent, at 3,247.71. Volume was very weak at 52.2 million shares.

Dealers said some investors were worried U.S. elections on Tuesday could shake-up U.S. markets and hurt Mexico. They also said some investors were keeping to the market sidelines until the Mexican government unveils its 1997 budget this week.
Traders put the recovery down to dealers picking up blue chips at what they felt were bargain prices.
"Volume was so low that it didn't take much buying to turn the IPC around. We did, however, recover ahead of the late surge in the Dow today," a Mexico-based trader said.
The Dow Jones meanwhile closed up 19.75 points, or 0.33 percent, at 6,041.68.
On the broad market, 95 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 36 to 33.
Debt-stricken holding company Sidek headed the gainers, up six centavos (1 cent) at 1.36 pesos (17 cents) on a rebound from last week's losses.
Autoparts maker Iasasa headed the losers, down three centavos (1 cent) at 45 centavos (6 cents) after what traders said had been a volatile performance in recent weeks.
Market heavyweight Telmex L shares slipped eight centavos (1 cent) to 12.12 pesos ($1.53).
Technical analysts situated support and resistance at 3,217 and 3,256 points, respectively.
